MUJAHID:v1p301#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p301#2/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
MUJAHID:v1p301#2/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya relates that Gabriel told the Prophet to give his community glad news of women, religion, status, victory, and power; Gabriel then warned that one who does afterlife deeds for worldly gain will have no share of them in the afterlife, and the Prophet responded with the formula of return to God.

MUQATIL:11:15-16/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:15-16/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:15-16/r1.claim: The verse concerns wicked people whose good deeds seek worldly life rather than God's approval; God fully gives them worldly reward in provision and benefit.

MUQATIL:11:15-16/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:15-16/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:15-16/r2.claim: Their worldly reward is not reduced, but this teaching is abrogated by the statement in 17:18 that God grants only what he wills to whom he wills.

FARRA:v2p6/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p6/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p6/r1.claim: A believer who seeks only this world's reward receives it promptly and without reduction in this world.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p302#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p302#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p302#3/r1.claim: Those whose sole aim is worldly life receive enough wealth and livelihood in it as recompense for their deeds, without being wronged.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p302#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p302#3/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p302#3/r2.claim: The Prophet said that a benefactor's good deed earns its reward from God in this world and the next.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p302#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p302#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p302#3/r3.claim: Mujahid says the one who seeks worldly life is repaid with a worldly reward, while his deeds are not accepted as lasting reward.

AKHFASH:v1p381/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p381/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p381/r1.claim: كان is jussive in the conditional, with نوف as its response.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p202#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p202#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p202#5/r1.claim: Those who seek worldly life and its adornment receive recompense for their deeds in this life without being shortchanged.

TUSTARI:11:15/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:11:15/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:11:15/r1.claim: Whoever seeks worldly status through knowledge receives the reward for the work in this life but nothing in the next, because the work was not sincere for God.

TUSTARI:11:15/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:11:15/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:11:15/r2.claim: If a person knew God had subjected the world and its people to seekers of the afterlife, he would not display his knowledge for show.

TUSTARI:11:15/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:11:15/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:11:15/r3.claim: Sincerity is the hardest thing for the ego because it has no share in it.

TUSTARI:11:15/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:11:15/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:11:15/r4.claim: Even faith, the root of religious duties, can be corrupted by showing off and become hypocrisy; deeds are still more vulnerable.

TUSTARI:11:15/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:11:15/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:11:15/r5.claim: A show-off is someone whose outward conduct escapes blame while God knows that the inward state contradicts it.

TAB-FULL:v12p347/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p347/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p347/r1.claim: Those who do good deeds seeking worldly life and its adornment receive their full reward in this life without being shortchanged.

TAB-FULL:v12p347/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p347/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v12p347/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says such people receive worldly benefits for good deeds done only for worldly ends, such as prayer or night worship, while their work for the afterlife is lost.

TAB-FULL:v12p347/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p347/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v12p347/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the worldly reward for good performed is paid in this world, while the next verse says such people have only the Fire and their work is void.

TAB-FULL:v12p347/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p347/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p347/r4.claim: Mujahid says that prayer or charity done without seeking God's face is paid back in this world in proportion to what was spent, with no afterlife reward.

TAB-FULL:v12p349/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r1.claim: Mujahid says people whose deeds are not accepted are given their recompense or have it hastened to them in this world.

TAB-FULL:v12p349/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r2.claim: Qatada says someone whose sole aim and intention is worldly life receives payment for good deeds here, leaving no good deed for which to be rewarded in the afterlife; believers receive reward in both.

TAB-FULL:v12p349/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r3.claim: Qatada explains لا يبخسون to mean they are not wronged in the afterlife; in another wording, God gives worldly wealth and livelihood as full recompense to the one seeking only this world.

TAB-FULL:v12p349/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r4.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the reward of one who does good for a benefactor rests with God in both the immediate world and the afterlife.

TAB-FULL:v12p349/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says nonbelievers may receive worldly recompense for righteous acts such as kinship, charity, and relieving distress, but have no share in the afterlife.

TAB-FULL:v12p349/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v12p349/r6.claim: The worldly reward can include expanded livelihood, contentment with possessions, and protection from worldly hardships.

TAB-FULL:v12p350/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p350/r1.speaker: أنس
TAB-FULL:v12p350/r1.claim: Anas says this verse concerns Jews and Christians.

TAB-FULL:v12p350/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p350/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v12p350/r2.claim: Al-Hasan glosses their recompense as their worldly good things or pleasures.

TAB-FULL:v12p350/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p350/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p350/r3.claim: Mujahid, as conveyed by Wahb, identifies the people seeking worldly reward as people of ostentation.

TAB-FULL:v12p351/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p351/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v12p351/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that on Judgment Day God will expose a Qur'an reciter, a wealthy giver, and a martyr who acted to be called learned, generous, or brave; despite those reputations, they will be first to fuel Hell.

TAB-FULL:v12p351/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p351/r2.speaker: معاوية
TAB-FULL:v12p351/r2.claim: After hearing Abu Hurayra's report, Muʿawiya wept and affirmed its truth by reciting this verse through the statement that their deeds are void.

TAB-FULL:v12p353/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p353/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p353/r1.claim: Mujahid says deeds such as fasting and prayer are not accepted when performed for worldly gain; such people receive their reward here and turn away from the afterlife, yet are not shortchanged in that reward.

ZAJJAJ:v3p42/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p42/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p42/r1.claim: Those seeking worldly life are repaid fully for their deeds in this life.

ZAJJAJ:v3p42/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p42/r2.speaker: أبو العباس محمد بن يزيد
ZAJJAJ:v3p42/r2.claim: Abu al-ʿAbbās says kāna is strong enough to stand for past or other actions, as in ‘if you had said it, He knew it’; the author describes it as reporting a state in past time, with yakūnu reporting a future state.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r1.claim: Qatada, reporting from Anas, says this verse was revealed about Jews and Christians.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the verse concerns someone doing worldly work without seeking God; he links it to 30:39, which says usury gains no reward from God.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r3.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r3.claim: Ali affirms that the passage describes someone who wants this world and does not want the Hereafter.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God pays worldly seekers in full for good works done solely to gain worldly benefit, such as prayer or fasting, without shortchanging them.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says even polytheists who perform charitable acts receive their recompense in this world, including for kinship, almsgiving, and helping the distressed.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r6.claim: Hasan interprets the worldly seeker as someone wanting to receive his good deeds' reward immediately.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r1.claim: Hasan interprets the world's adornments as its good and pleasant things.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God gives worldly seekers the recompense they pursued in this life.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r3.claim: Mujahid says God hastens reward for the person whose deeds will not be accepted in the Hereafter.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says God hastens such a person's reward in the world through expanded provision, contentment, and relief from hardship, leaving no share in the Hereafter.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r5.claim: Qatada says the world-focused person receives reward for good deeds in this life but reaches the Hereafter with none; a believer receives reward in both lives and is not wronged.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r6.claim: Qatada glosses not being shortchanged as not being wronged.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses not being shortchanged as not being diminished.

NAHHAS:v2p273/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p273/r3.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v2p273/r3.claim: Mujahid says good deeds are rewarded in this world; Maymun says believers are repaid in both worlds and disbelievers in this one.

SULAMI:v1p315/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p315/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v1p315/r1.claim: Worldly life consists of pursuing wishes and desires, roaming through hopes, forgetting sudden death, and amassing wealth by lawful or unlawful means; its adornment includes wealth and human attachments.

SULAMI:v1p315/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p315/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p315/r2.claim: Wanting worldly life means disliking death, and every doubter is fearful.

SULAMI:v1p315/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p315/r3.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v1p315/r3.claim: Worldly life is intimacy and attachment to worldly people; loving it means loving what God hates, and such company turns one from the Real's path because the world is play and amusement.

THALABI:v5p160/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p160/r3.claim: Those who seek worldly life and its adornment through their deeds are repaid fully in this life, without shortfall.

THALABI:v5p160/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v5p160/r4.claim: Qatada says a person whose aim, joy, desire, and intention are worldly receives the reward of good deeds here but has none left to repay in the Hereafter.

THALABI:v5p160/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p160/r5.claim: A believer may receive good deeds’ rewards in both worlds, unlike the person whose worldly aim exhausts the reward in this life.

THALABI:v5p160/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160/r6.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p160/r6.claim: The Prophet says whoever does good for someone receives their reward from God in both the immediate world and the Hereafter.

THALABI:v5p160/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p160/r7.claim: One disagreement says the verse concerns unbelievers; believers intend both worlds, with their intention for the Hereafter prevailing, as the next verse indicates.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r1.claim: كان is treated as semantically redundant; the conditional means whoever wants worldly life, so its جواب نوف is jussive.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r10.claim: In al-Kalbī's report through Abū Ṣāliḥ, the passage was revealed about people of the qibla.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r11.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r11.claim: The people described are those who act for show.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r2.claim: Reporting al-Mubarrad, كان and تكون can describe states in both past and future; here the condition concerns the future, as in يكن.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r3.claim: The conditional means whoever wants worldly life; the verb كان is understood in a future condition as يكن.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r4.claim: Zuhayr's line illustrates the conditional use of a past-form verb with present or future meaning: whoever fears death's causes will meet them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r5.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, those seeking immediate worldly life reject resurrection, reward, and punishment; this makes the passage about unbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r6.claim: One whose sole concern is worldly life receives recompense for good deeds here, then reaches the afterlife without a good deed to reward; believers are rewarded in both.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r7.claim: Some exegetes apply the verses to unbelievers because of the following verse: believers seek both worlds, with the afterlife their greater aim.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r8.claim: On this reading, an unbeliever's good acts such as feeding, clothing, and defending oppressed Muslims are repaid through worldly prosperity and comforts.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r9.claim: The unbelievers receive their good deeds' reward in this world and have only the Fire in the afterlife, where they regret having no good deed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r1.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r1.claim: A believer who performs a righteous act without God-consciousness is given its reward in this world.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ adopts the view that a person of the qibla who intends worldly reward is paid fully in this life, without any shortfall.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r3.claim: The Prophet describes ostentatious reciters, spenders, and fighters, who acted to earn reputations, as the first people whose Fire is kindled on Judgment Day.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r4.speaker: معاوية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r4.claim: After hearing the report, Muʿāwiya wept, affirmed that God and His Messenger spoke truth, and recited these two verses.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r5.claim: The warning concerns Muslims whose good acts serve worldly aims without thought of the afterlife; they receive worldly recompense but face punishment if they did not seek God's approval and reward.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r7.claim: The verse's wording appears to say that ostentation and worldly intent without seeking afterlife reward invalidate faith at death, since “their deeds were null” includes faith and its branches.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r1.claim: This concerns unbelievers who want worldly life but do not believe in resurrection, reward, or punishment; they receive full worldly recompense for good acts.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r2.claim: Examples of such good deeds are feeding the hungry, clothing the unclothed, and supporting an oppressed Muslim; their reward comes as increased wealth in this life.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r3.claim: They are not shortchanged in worldly recompense, but arrive in the afterlife with regret because they have no good deeds there.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r1.claim: Tawfiya means fully delivering what is due; the related forms with or without doubling mean the same, though doubling is more emphatic.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say a disbeliever may maintain kinship, give to a beggar, or help someone in distress and receive worldly reward through expanded provision or averted harm.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r2.claim: Bakhs is a shortfall in what is due; every oppressor is a defrauder because injustice reduces another's right.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r3.claim: The word kāna in من كان may be extra with the meaning whoever wants, mean came to be, or form a construction like the example about a shirt.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r4.claim: نوف إليهم is the response to the condition: whoever intends worldly life will have their deeds repaid fully here.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r5.speaker: الأصم وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r5.claim: They say the verse was revealed about disbelievers.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the verse was revealed about hypocrites.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid says it was revealed about people who deal in usury.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r8.claim: Because pursuit of worldly adornment can deter people from religion, those who seek only this life receive the full recompense of their deeds in it, without shortchanging; in the hereafter they have only the Fire and their deeds are null.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r9.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r9.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the verse concerns polytheists who do good deeds such as maintaining kinship or avoiding injustice without believing in resurrection; their deeds are rejected because they were not done in worship of God, yet they receive their full worldly provision and lifespan.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p165#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p165#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p165#2/r4.claim: The verse concerns those who do deeds seeking worldly life and its adornment, including anyone who acts for other than God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p165#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p165#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p165#2/r5.claim: God fully pays them in this life through ample provision and repelling hardship, without reducing their worldly share.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r1.claim: Those who seek worldly life receive the full wages of their deeds in this world, including health and provision, without any reduction.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r2.claim: One view identifies them as ostentatious people: reciters, charitable kin-keepers, and fighters each sought a reputation and got it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r3.claim: Anas says they are Jews and Christians: charitable giving and kinship earned them immediate reward through greater provision and bodily health.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r4.claim: Another view says they are hypocrites who joined the Prophet's campaigns and received a share of the spoils.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p364/r5.claim: Readings include يوف with yāʾ, making God the subject; تُوفَ with tāʾ in the passive; and al-Hasan's light نوفي with yāʾ because the conditional verb is past.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r4.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r4.claim: They take the universal wording about seeking worldly life as specifically referring to disbelievers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r5.claim: Mujahid includes disbelievers and believers who act for show; Muawiya adopted this after Shafi ibn Mati al-Asbahi relayed the Prophetic report about a charity-giver, slain fighter, and Qur'an-reciter whose ostentation makes them first fuel for Hell, then wept and cited the passage.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r6.claim: For the disbeliever reading, يريد means to intend and aim: worldly life is the person's sole goal, without belief in an afterlife; God repays good deeds with worldly favors, though provision may be narrow or ample, and their afterlife is only Fire.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the disbeliever interpretation because the preceding context concerns those opposing the Qur'an.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r2.claim: On the view that the passage includes sinful believers, يريد means love, prefer, and choose; God rewards good deeds not done for Him with worldly favors, while 'only Fire' means it is what they deserve, though God may forgive them.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r3.claim: Anas says the verses concern the People of the Book; Ibn Atiyya says they are included as disbelievers, not the exclusive referent.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r4.claim: The majority read نوف with the majestic first-person nūn; Talha and Maymun ibn Mihran read يوف with a third-person yāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r5.claim: يبخسون means they are given less than their reward.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r7.claim: The pronoun in فيها first refers to worldly life and in its third occurrence to the afterlife; alternatives make all three refer to this world or the second to deeds.

TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r1.claim: The verse also states that people who pursue this world have no share in the hereafter.

TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r2.claim: The Prophetic report promises the community worldly honor and establishment, while warning that deeds done for worldly aims bring no afterlife share.

TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r7.claim: The connection answers whether outwardly professing Islam for worldly safety suffices: worldly seeking, by profession or other means, leads to this outcome.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r10.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:11:15-16/r10.claim: Al-Jubba'i applies it to hypocrites who joined the Prophet's campaigns for booty rather than religious support, receiving a share of the spoils as their recompense.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16/r11.claim: A further view applies it to people who perform good deeds ostentatiously, earning no afterlife reward.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16/r3.claim: Zina is improvement through clothing, jewelry, or appearance; tawfiya is paying a right in full, and bakhs is withholding part of someone's due.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16/r4.claim: The proverb about a woman who is both thought foolish and a defrauder illustrates bakhs as the shortchanging of another's right.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r5.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:11:15-16/r5.claim: Al-Farra' treats كان as an extra particle here, yielding the sense 'whoever wants worldly life.'

TABRISI:11:15-16/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:15-16/r6.claim: Abu Ali argues that a conditional clause and its result refer only to the future, so the conditional particle converts a past verb's meaning to future; لو can instead retain past reference without jussive marking.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16/r7.claim: The address concerns people seeking worldly life's bloom and beauty without the hereafter; God gives them their deeds' full recompense in this world without shortchanging them.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r8.speaker: الضحاك، قتادة، ابن عباس
TABRISI:11:15-16/r8.claim: These authorities apply it to resurrection-denying polytheists who do good by kinship, charity, avoiding oppression, aiding victims, and rationally commendable works; God repays them with worldly provision, health, enjoyment, and protection from hardship.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16/r9.claim: If such a disbeliever dies before receiving full worldly compensation, God reduces the amount of punishment in the hereafter accordingly, but grants no hereafter reward.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r1.claim: The promise concerns everyone who seeks worldly life and its adornment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r2.claim: Another view makes it about Muslims, the people of the qibla.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r3.speaker: أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r3.claim: Another view identifies Jews and Christians.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r4.claim: Another view identifies people who act for show.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r5.claim: The intended person seeks immediate worldly gain while rejecting resurrection and recompense; another explanation restricts the verse to unbelievers because believers seek both lives.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r6.claim: God fully repays their deeds by giving them their reward in worldly life.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p83#3/r7.claim: Someone who gives charity or maintains kinship without seeking God's pleasure receives that recompense in this world, which also averts worldly harm.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p84/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p84/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p84/r1.claim: “While they are in it” means in this world.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p84/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p84/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p84/r2.claim: They are not shortchanged of their deeds' reward in worldly life.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r1.claim: The opponents claimed to dispute with Muhammad to establish truth, but Rāzī says envy and refusal to follow him were their real motives.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r2.claim: The verse resembles 17:18 and 42:20, which distinguish those seeking worldly life from those seeking the harvest of the hereafter.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r3.claim: One view restricts the verse to disbelievers because its ending about hell and nullified deeds cannot describe believers generally; the general opening is narrowed to those seeking only worldly adornment.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r4.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r4.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the disbelievers who deny resurrection are intended, since they desire only worldly happiness.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r5.claim: Another view identifies hypocrites who joined the Prophet's campaigns to seek spoils without belief in afterlife reward.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r6.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r6.claim: A third view, transmitted from Anas, identifies Jews and Christians.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r7.claim: The Qāḍī's chosen reading concerns people who do good deeds for worldly praise: social benefits such as charity and public works benefit others, but worship without proper intention is not obedience.

RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r1.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r1.claim: On the Qāḍī's view, the deeds meant are good works that a disbeliever can validly perform.

RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r2.claim: A second view takes the wording generally, including believers who act for reputation and disbelievers who seek worldly reward; the hell clause is difficult unless it means punishment for those corrupted acts.

RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits a prophetic report that the Qurʾān reciter, wealthy donor, and martyr are condemned because each sought public praise rather than God.

RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r4.claim: After Abū Hurayra recited this report to Muʿāwiya, the narrator says Muʿāwiya wept and then affirmed the truth of the verse.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r1.claim: The verse’s rule that reward follows intention means a Ramadan fast not intended as the Ramadan fast does not count, nor does washing for cooling count as prayer ablution; the principle extends to similar acts.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r2.claim: Most scholars take this verse and similar statements in al-Shura and Ali Imran as unrestricted, then qualified by the verse on the immediate life: God grants what He wills to whomever He wills.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that this verse was abrogated by the verse about whoever desires the immediate life.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r4.claim: Qurtubi rejects abrogation here and prefers an unrestricted-versus-qualified reading; an apparently universal promise of answering prayer is similarly qualified by God’s will.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15#2/r5.claim: Abrogating statements of fact is impossible because truths cannot change and God cannot lie; reports about legal rulings may be abrogated, subject to scholarly debate.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r1.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r1.claim: Al-Farra’ treats kāna as extra, explaining the jussive response in the verse.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads man kāna as a jussive condition with nuwaf as its answer, meaning whoever wants; the shift from past to future is supported by Zuhayr’s poetry.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r3.speaker: الضحاك والنحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse concerns disbelievers, and al-Nahhas prefers this because the next verse denies them any afterlife share beyond the Fire; worldly charity earns health and wealth only.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r4.claim: Another view applies it to believers who intend only worldly reward: they receive full worldly recompense but punishment in the afterlife because their purpose was confined to this world.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r5.claim: A report about show-offs says they fasted, prayed, gave charity, fought, and recited to gain praise, and will be among the first fuel of Hell; Abu Hurayra wept, affirmed it, and recited these verses.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r6.speaker: مجاهد وميمون بن مهران
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r6.claim: Mujahid and Maymun ibn Mihran apply the verse generally to anyone who intends something other than God, whether or not the person has basic faith.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r7.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r7.claim: Maymun says every good deed is repaid: a sincere Muslim receives reward in this world and the next, while a disbeliever receives it in this world alone.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:15/r8.claim: A narrower view concerns people who joined the Prophet’s campaign for worldly spoils; Qurtubi rejects that limitation and prefers the general reading.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:15/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:15/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:15/r1.claim: People seeking worldly life through benevolence receive its worldly recompense, such as health, leadership, abundant provision, and many children, without any reduction.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:15/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:15/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:15/r2.claim: The verb has readings with a third-person subject, passive voice, lightening, or indicative mood; a poem illustrates the indicative form after a past conditional.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:15/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:15/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:15/r3.claim: The verse may concern show-offs, hypocrites, or disbelievers whose stated purpose is worldly recompense and benevolence.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p149/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p149/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p149/r1.claim: Those seeking worldly life and its adornment receive their full wages in this world, including provision and health, without being shortchanged; they are unbelievers or hypocrites.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p149/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p149/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p149/r2.claim: The people receiving this worldly recompense are identified as unbelievers or hypocrites.

QASHANI:11:15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:15/r1.claim: Anyone whose work, even apparently religious, intends worldly advantage receives its full recompense here and none in the afterlife.

QASHANI:11:15/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:15/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:15/r2.claim: Each person has a worldly share from constitution and an afterlife share from innate nature; turning wholly to the lower world makes it a veil, reverses fitra, and recruits the heart to serve the ego.

QASHANI:11:15/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:15/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:15/r3.claim: They are not shortchanged in worldly reward because the heart, molded into the ego's form, receives its share in the ego's image.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r1.claim: After mentioning contradictions about revelation, the passage turns to the worldly course and final outcome of unbelievers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r2.claim: The wording is general for anyone seeking worldly adornment, but reward remains subject to God’s will, as in the verse about the immediate life.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r3.claim: Mujahid applies the warning to unbelievers and believers who perform deeds for show.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r4.speaker: معونة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r4.claim: The source says Maʿuna, after hearing the Prophet’s statement about show-offs, recited this verse.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r5.speaker: أنس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r5.claim: Anas applies the verse to Jews and Christians; Ibn ʿAtiyya says they are included without being its only referents. Another view applies it to hypocrites who fought alongside the Messenger and received a share of spoils.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r6.claim: The intent is apparently righteous deeds done solely for worldly gain without belief in the afterlife; God repays unbelievers’ good deeds in this life.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r7.claim: He illustrates ostentation through conspicuous, lengthened prayer, public charity for praise, and displaying knowledge for worldly standing; concealed charity is the contrast, as in a prophetic report.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p131#2/r8.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAli reads إنما نزل with doubled nūn and zāy; ما may be a verbal noun or a relative pronoun with an omitted object.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r1.claim: Most readers have نوف; Talha ibn Maymun reads يوف in third person, Zayd ibn ʿAli reads a light يوف, and passive تُوَفْ with nominative أعمالهم is also reported.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r2.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ calls كان extra to explain the jussive response; the author objects that يريد would then need jussive marking and that a past condition can take a present response without كان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reads نوفي with light fāʾ and retained yāʾ; it may be jussive with an estimated vowel in a dialect or indicative as in a poem.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says ostentatious people receive in this world the reward for good deeds done solely for worldly gain, such as fasting, prayer, or night vigil, but their work is void in the Hereafter; Mujahid and al-Dahhak also report this view.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r2.claim: Anas and Hasan say these verses were revealed about Jews and Christians.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and others identify the people addressed as those who act for show.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r4.claim: Qatada says those whose goal and intention are worldly receive their good deeds' reward here, then arrive with no rewarded good deed; believers are rewarded both here and in the Hereafter.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p511#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p511#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p511#2/r7.claim: Those whose deeds seek worldly life and adornment receive their full worldly recompense, such as status and wealth, without reduction; their bodies, souls, and religions are still impoverished in both worlds.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p511#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p511#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p511#2/r8.claim: This worldly recompense explains why punishment is withheld during their period of respite despite their wrongdoing.

DURR-FULL:v4p405/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r6.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r6.claim: Anas says the promise about those seeking worldly life and its adornment was revealed concerning Jews and Christians.

DURR-FULL:v4p405/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن معبد
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r7.claim: In response to a question to Ali, the verse concerns a person who wants worldly life and seeks no Hereafter.

DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the desired life as its reward and adornment as its wealth; God fully grants health, family joy, money, and children, a rule he says was abrogated by 17:18.

DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r1.claim: The Prophet describes three groups among his community: sincere worshippers enter Paradise, while those who worship for worldly gain or to be seen are sent to Hell.

DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says hypocritical people will see Paradise's scent and palaces, then be denied its reward and taste painful punishment because they performed before people but disregarded God in private.

DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.claim: The worldly seeker receives the reward of his deed here but nothing in the Hereafter; Sa'id compares this to the verse about usury not growing with God.

DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r4.claim: Qatada says whoever makes worldly life his sole concern is repaid good deeds here but has no good in the Hereafter; a believer may be rewarded in both worlds, without being wronged.

DURR-FULL:v4p407/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r1.claim: Al-Suddi gives the same interpretation that worldly seekers receive what they seek in this life.

DURR-FULL:v4p407/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says even prayer, fasting, and night worship can be done to obtain worldly benefit; its seeker receives that benefit, but the deed is null and he loses in the Hereafter.

DURR-FULL:v4p407/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr defines the person as one who acts for worldly gain without seeking God.

DURR-FULL:v4p407/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse was revealed about the polytheists.

DURR-FULL:v4p407/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies the people described as those who show off in worship.

DURR-FULL:v4p407/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r6.claim: The Prophet says the first judged include a Qur'an reciter, a wealthy donor, and a slain fighter; each is condemned because he acted for public praise and is sent to Hell. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan.

DURR-FULL:v4p408/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r1.claim: Mujahid says one who works for worldly gain without seeking God receives the full recompense for that work in this life.

DURR-FULL:v4p408/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r2.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r2.claim: A person's standing with God is reflected in their deeds; the believer may be rewarded in both worlds, while the unbeliever receives worldly reward only.

DURR-FULL:v4p408/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r3.claim: Hasan glosses the works fully repaid in worldly life as the person's good and pleasant things.

DURR-FULL:v4p408/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they receive every worldly pleasure promptly and are not wronged by what was not expedited, since they sought only this life.

DURR-FULL:v4p408/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r5.claim: Mujahid says worldly recompense is hastened for the person whose deed will not be accepted.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r1.claim: The verse describes those whose good-looking deeds seek worldly life and its adornments, such as health, security, wealth, children, and status, with كَان suggesting persistent intent and little concern for the afterlife.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r2.claim: They receive the full recompense of their deeds in this life; the phrase omits a genitive meaning their rewards, rather than using deeds metaphorically for rewards.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r3.claim: The verb نوف includes the sense of conveying, which explains its construction with إلى even though it normally takes a direct object.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r4.speaker: طلحة بن ميمون
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r4.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn Maymūn reads يوف with yāʾ and the verb attributed to God; Zayd ibn ʿAlī uses a light form, and a passive reading raises أعمالهم.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads نوفي without the final yāʾ in the jussive, explained through Arabic deletion patterns or the weakened force of a distant conditional response.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r6.speaker: الفَرّاء
ALUSI-FULL:v12p23#2/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says كان is extra and accounts for the jussive response; Abū Ḥayyān objects that the actual conditional verb يريد would then have to be jussive.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r1.claim: لا يبخسون means their worldly recompense is not reduced; the pronoun most naturally refers to worldly life, though another view refers it to the deeds.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r2.claim: The wording presents full recompense as payment of a right and non-reduction as avoiding injustice, although the recipients have no claim to it; the promise remains governed by God's wise will.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r3.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib defines bakhs as an unjust reduction, which heightens the denial of any shortfall.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is quoted by al-Naḥḥās as saying that the verse of worldly recompense abrogated the present verse; al-Ālūsī says abrogation of reports is impossible and treats the statement as loose usage.

ELMALILI:11:15/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:15/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:15/r1.claim: The verse concerns people whose sole intention is worldly life and its adornment, and who work toward that end.

ELMALILI:11:15/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:15/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:15/r2.claim: God fully repays such people’s deeds in this world: their effort is not shorted or delayed, and they receive at least the value of their work. This does not mean every desired outcome is granted, since the promise concerns deeds, not wishes.

ELMALILI:11:15/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:15/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:15/r3.claim: People are created to compete and be tested in deeds, and every act yields a good or bad consequence; the author links this to the promise that effort will be seen.

ELMALILI:11:15/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:15/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:15/r4.claim: A diver may fail to find the pearl sought but still accomplish the dive, learning the skill or suffering an accident; the true fruit is the outcome God assigns to the act.

ELMALILI:11:15/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:15/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:15/r5.claim: Because those whose highest aim is transient worldly life have exhausted their deeds’ reward within this life, their recompense cannot extend into the everlasting hereafter.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r1.claim: This parenthetical warning follows the challenge to submit: if people seek worldly rank instead of truth, their worldly enjoyment ends in lasting punishment; the second clause is the main point.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r2.claim: The warning explains resistance to faith and cautions Muslims not to mistake unbelievers' worldly ease for divine approval or assume disbelief brings immediate punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r1.claim: The Prophet renounced much luxury and adornment, framing the women choice as a question of lifestyle.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r2.claim: The Prophet's wives' choice of worldly life means comfort and clothing, not rejecting the afterlife, so it concerns a different sense of worldly adornment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r3.claim: The pronoun “to them” refers to the people described by the relative clause.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r4.claim: God gives their chosen worldly works in full by leaving them free of faith's burdens; believers forgo some enjoyment to obey God and avoid its afterlife consequences.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r5.claim: The verb “complete” takes ila because it also conveys “deliver” or “bring,” allowing both senses.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r6.claim: The verse does not promise every desire to whoever wants worldly life: it says their works are completed and left to them without the burdens of faith.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r1.claim: They are not deprived of worldly blessings as punishment for unbelief; God leaves them to their lot as respite and gradual enticement, showing unbelief does not bar divine blessing.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r2.claim: The pronoun “in it” may refer either to worldly life or to their works.

TABATABAI:11:15-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:15-16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:15-16/r3.claim: Tawfiya means delivering someone’s due in full, while bakhs is reduction of recompense.

TABATABAI:11:15-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:15-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:15-16/r4.claim: Those who choose worldly life receive the worldly results they seek when other causes cooperate; deeds produce the goal for which they were intended, while unintentional good works earn no afterlife reward.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Quraysh argued that the Prophet’s and his companions’ poverty disproved prophethood, while their own wealth suggested God favored them rather than threatened them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Worldly pleasures are not rewards for good deeds; God gives them to both virtuous people and wrongdoers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Without the Hereafter, this world itself is a baseless creation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Actions focused wholly on this world are baseless even when an undertaking appears pious.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Those seeking worldly pleasures receive only what God wills and in whatever quantity divine authority and wisdom decide.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Hereafter-directed effort counts only when done with faith, sincerity, and fitting righteous action; ostentation, shirk, and verbal claims to Paradise have no value.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r1.claim: God does not leave anyone’s work unrewarded: people receive returns in the fields where they develop their God-given abilities, as 3:145 also says.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r2.claim: Those who disbelieve in the afterlife and use their abilities only for worldly pleasure, security, wealth, influence, and display receive their full return in this life, but their only afterlife outcome is Hell.

STUDYQURAN:11:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r1.claim: The warning concerns those who want only worldly life and deny the Hereafter; lawful enjoyment of this world can also apply to believers.

STUDYQURAN:11:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r2.claim: Some read the promise as God hastening believers’ reward for righteous aims in this world without reducing their Hereafter reward.

STUDYQURAN:11:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r3.claim: One reported occasion is that the verse concerned believers in the Prophet’s time whose religious acts were driven by ostentation.

STUDYQURAN:11:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r5.claim: Some invoke the hadith that actions are judged according to intentions in explaining the fate of deeds.
